summary: Embedding bulk upload causing elevated 5xx (502/504) from API gateway; correlated with GPU driver resets and keepalive drops
description:
Issue summary:
Aurelius Health reports a sustained elevation in 5xx responses (502/504) on their embedding bulk upload route starting ~2026-03-13 10:45 PDT. Errors surface at the API gateway with upstream resets.

Impact:
- Customer embedding ingestion failing for ~40% of requests during peak upload window (10:30-11:20 PDT).
- Affects a single dedicated tenant pool for Aurelius Health; customer reports failed uploads in production, blocking nightly ETL.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool: ded-pool-az2-usw2 (GPU nodes: A100-80GB, driver image: nvidia-driver:525.89)
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer issues large embedding batch (multipart/streamed) of ~250k vectors via /v1/embeddings:batch endpoint
2) Requests stream concurrently from 8 worker processes (concurrency ~64), each using keepalive connections
3) After ~10-15 minutes of sustained throughput, API gateway begins returning 502 and 504s; upstream runtime logs show NVML reset messages and abrupt worker exits
observed_behavior: Sequence of events observed in metrics and logs: (a) api-gateway accept queue grows; (b) keepalive timeouts increase; (c) serving-runtime reports 'NVML: GPU reset' and 'watchdog: runtime exit' followed by rapid restarts; (d) Autoscaler attempts to replace failed pods but new pods receive the same uploads and also fail, amplifying 5xx rate.
logs_and_metrics: runtime stderr: 'NVML: GPU reset detected on device 0'
node dmesg: 'GPU hang: ch 0 faulted; forced reset'
serving-runtime: OOM not observed; CPU steady ~70%, but GPU reset correlates with 99th latency spikes
netstat: listen backlog rising from 128 -> 1024 within 90s during the event
keepalive/conn metrics: active keepalive count drops; handshakes increase 5x
workarounds_applied: 1) Throttled customer's ingestion to concurrency 16 and reduced per-worker streams to 2 (immediate reduction in 5xx to <5%).
2) Temporarily routed Aurelius Health traffic to warm spare dedicated pool (ded-pool-az2-usw2-spare) with older driver image (nvidia-driver:520.78) — success for short window.
3) Customer committed to staggering uploads (5 minute cooldown between batches) pending root cause fix.
comments: Maya Chen (Support) 2026-03-13T11:12:00Z: Initial report received from Aurelius Health. Asked for request IDs, timestamps, and whether uploads are compressed/multipart. Escalated to SRE due to GPU reset logs.

Luis Ortega (SRE) 2026-03-13T11:28:00Z: Observed NVML reset traces on 3 different runtime nodes in ded-pool-az2-usw2. Correlation window matches customer's bulk ingestion. Opening investigation; tagging runtime/driver teams.

Priya Nambiar (Runtime Eng) 2026-03-13T12:05:00Z: Noted driver image 525.89 in pool. Past incidents showed intermittent hangs under heavy pci-bandwidth + multipart streaming. Spun up spare pool with 520.78 for repro.
Aurelius Health (Customer) 2026-03-13T12:22:30Z: Confirmed reduced concurrency workaround improved success rate for recent batch. Requesting ETA for permanent fix and whether this will recur.

Luis Ortega (SRE) 2026-03-13T13:40:00Z: Autoscaler behavior contributed to amplification: new nodes immediately received queued uploads and hit the same driver hang. Plan: implement short ingress-queue drain + retry-backoff to avoid stampede during restarts.

Maya Chen (Support) 2026-03-14T09:15:00Z: Customer notified of temporary mitigations and scheduled maintenance window for driver upgrade on 2026-03-15 02:00 UTC. Provided checklist and expected downtime ~3-5 minutes per node.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis A: Recent nvidia driver 525.89 has a regression under sustained multi-process CUDA context churn with large streaming uploads leading to GPU hangs and NVML resets.
Hypothesis B: Combined effect of high accept-queue/backlog on API gateway + immediate fanout to busy GPUs causes increased PCIe contention and triggers existing driver corner case.

Checked: No kernel OOMs, no container OOMs. NVML resets present in kernel logs across 4 different node instances in the pool. Memory fragmentation on GPU observed after ~12 minutes of sustained upload in stress tests.
Repro: Synthetic load runner reproduces GPU reset after ~9-12 minutes when running 64 concurrent small-stream embedding inserts on driver 525.89; not reproducible on 520.78 under same load.
Related PR: runtime change to gate immediate routing of queued requests to newly created pods is proposed (see PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4871) to reduce stampede.
Telemetry: Trace shows keepalive churn increases TLS handshake rate 4x before resets — indicates connection churn may exacerbate driver behavior due to sudden new cuda contexts.
resolution_notes: Short term: We applied per-tenant throttling and migrated Aurelius Health to a spare pool running driver 520.78 which restored normal success rates. Medium term: Scheduled driver rollout to driver 520.78 on ded-pool-az2-usw2 during maintenance window 2026-03-15 02:00 UTC. Long term: Runtime PR to implement ingress-queue drain and backoff on pod replacement merged and staged for canary (PR #4871). Postmortem and driver upgrade verification runbook linked. Customer asked for confirmation once stable; CS to follow up post-maintenance.
next_steps: 1) Perform staged driver downgrade on ded-pool-az2-usw2 in maintenance window (2026-03-15).
2) Canary PR #4871 in non-customer dedicated pools and observe accept-queue and pod-replacement behavior under synthetic load.
3) Create KB article for customers advising recommended ingest concurrency limits for large embedding uploads and the option to use spare pools if available.
4) Schedule postmortem with runtime/driver/infra teams and share to Aurelius Health within 48h of completion.
